title: Console: experiment results dashboard (variant deltas, charts) + query perf guards
author: Felix Schneider
release_notes: Console: Adds an experiment Results view with per-variant latency/cost/error deltas and guardrail status.
Console: Adds charting for p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, throughput, and cost/token over time (default 1h bucket).
Performance: Adds UI-side query guards and response caching to avoid expensive high-cardinality requests.
body: Summary: Implements the Console experiment Results dashboard used to monitor active and completed route experiments. The page consumes the results API introduced in pr-28644 and presents (1) guardrail status + banners, (2) KPI tiles with deltas vs control, and (3) time-series charts for latency, error rate, throughput, and cost/token. This PR also includes performance optimizations/guardrails specifically to prevent high-cardinality query explosions when users expand breakdowns by {route, model, region}. Motivation: During beta we saw two failure modes: (a) results appearing stale/confusing (SUP-24910) and (b) results queries becoming expensive when the UI naively requested too many series (see internal thread on results-query cost spike). This change defaults to a safe, fast summary view and requires explicit user intent to expand into higher-cardinality dimensions. Feature flag: All UI is gated behind `route_experiments_results_ui` (and still requires `route_experiments` account enablement). What’s in scope: Results landing section: headline status (Running/Stopped/Degraded), last-updated timestamp, config version (to correlate with propagation lag), and a persistent experiment header showing route + variant mapping. KPI tiles: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), error rate (%), throughput (rps), cost/token (usd / 1k tokens) and absolute cost (usd/hr), each with delta vs control and a tooltip describing the metric definition. Guardrails: a guardrail panel showing thresholds configured on the experiment plus current value; shows soft-stop vs hard-stop semantics (banner copy matches PM decision: soft-stop by default; hard-stop only if enabled). Charts: time-series for each metric; default window 24h, bucket 1h; supports 1h/6h/24h/7d windows with server-approved bucket sizes. Variant comparison: control vs treatment lines with consistent colors; optional “Show confidence band” is intentionally omitted (non-goal for GA). Drilldowns: optional breakdown toggles for Region and Model. These are off by default and gated by a “This may increase query cost” warning and a hard cap on series count. Performance changes (UI): Request coalescing: identical queries (same experiment_id, window, bucket, breakdown flags) are deduped in-flight so rapid UI interactions don’t fan out. Local response cache: 30s in-memory cache for the results payload keyed by query signature; reduces repeated refreshes when users flip between tabs. Safe defaults: no breakdown dimensions by default; region/model breakdown requires explicit toggle and is limited to top N (default 5) by traffic. Series caps: enforce a maximum number of time-series rendered; if exceeded, UI falls back to summary-only with a prompt to narrow scope. Pagination for tables: the per-variant “Top routes” and “Top errors” tables are paginated and do not auto-fetch all rows. Explicit refresh: auto-refresh every 60s while running, but only for summary query; expanded breakdowns do not auto-refresh unless user pins them. API usage notes: This PR uses `GET /console/experiments/:id/results` with query params `{window, bucket, breakdown}`. The UI prefers the pre-aggregated rollup path and only requests expanded breakdowns when toggled. It also surfaces the `data_freshness_lag_sec` field (if present) as “Updated X min ago” to help debug aggregation delays. UX notes: Copy and empty states reviewed with Design. If an experiment has insufficient traffic or results are not yet available (first few minutes), we show a clear empty state with guidance and a link to the relevant runbook for attribution drop / propagation lag. Tests: Adds unit tests for query signature caching + series cap logic; adds a Cypress smoke test for loading the results page behind the feature flag. Observability: Adds a client-side performance timer around results queries and logs a warning event when the UI hits a series cap (to help us detect misuse). Screenshots: Included in the PR description on GitHub (not in this JSON). Rollout plan: Merge behind flag, enable for internal accounts first, then beta allowlist. Follow-ups: (1) Add “quality/eval score” chart once the eval-score stream is stable for all beta accounts (tracked separately). (2) Consider server-enforced query limits aligned with UI caps.

results: add KPI tiles + delta formatting utilities
results-query: add request coalescing + 30s cache keyed by query signature

review_conversation: Chloe Martin: Can we avoid auto-refreshing the expanded breakdown query? That’s the one that can get expensive if someone leaves the page open.
Felix Schneider (author): Good call. Updated so only the summary query auto-refreshes. Expanded breakdowns require manual refresh or re-toggle.
Logan Wright: Please make sure the UI is not defaulting to route_id raw path. We need normalized template route IDs to keep cardinality sane.
Felix Schneider (author): Confirmed we’re using the `route_id` returned by the results API (normalized). Also added a tooltip for what route_id represents.
Allison Grant: The series cap behavior should be explicit. If we truncate to top 5, tell the user and provide a way to narrow scope.
Felix Schneider (author): Added an inline notice: “Showing top 5 by traffic” and a link to docs explaining breakdown cost/cardinality.
Alicia Perez: Charts look good, but the delta pills are hard to scan. Can we use consistent sign formatting and color only on the delta (not the whole tile)?
Felix Schneider (author): Updated delta styling: sign prefix (+/-), neutral color for base value, color only on delta; also improved contrast per design feedback.
Marissa Cole: Please align banner copy with the soft-stop vs hard-stop decision. GA promise is soft-stop by default with optional hard-stop when enabled.
Felix Schneider (author): Updated banner copy and added a tooltip explaining the behavior. Also ensured we show whether hard-stop is enabled on the experiment.
Marissa Cole: Approved once the feature flag is confirmed off by default.
Felix Schneider (author): Confirmed flag default is false; requires allowlist. Pushed a small follow-up commit to ensure it’s not accidentally enabled in dev presets.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash merge by Felix Schneider
